title: Post-training quantization and the critical dataset size
goal: Section 3.1 models the loss that post-training quantization (PTQ) adds as $\delta_{\text{PTQ}} = C_T \, D^{\gamma_D} N^{-\gamma_N} e^{-P_{\text{post}}/\gamma_{\text{post}}}$ (Equation 2). Write `delta_ptq(n, d, p_post)`, which returns it. The constants of Appendix K, Table 2 are defined in the starter. Then write `d_crit(n, p_post)`, which returns the token count $D_{\text{crit}}$ where $B D^{-\beta} + \delta_{\text{PTQ}}$ stops falling, so that more pretraining data raises the loss of the quantized model (Appendix E.1, Equations 12 and 13).
hints: `delta_ptq` is one line. The exponents differ: $D$ gets $\gamma_D = 0.5068$ and $N$ gets $\gamma_N = 0.3439$. Check: for $N = 30$M, $D = 26$B, and 4 bits, the result is about 0.0349.

To find $D_{\text{crit}}$, set the derivative of $B D^{-\beta} + \delta_{\text{PTQ}}$ with respect to $D$ to zero: $\beta B D^{-\beta - 1} = \gamma_D C_T N^{-\gamma_N} e^{-P_{\text{post}}/\gamma_{\text{post}}} D^{\gamma_D - 1}$.

Collect the powers of $D$ on one side. They combine to $D^{\gamma_D + \beta}$, which gives $D_{\text{crit}} = \left(\dfrac{\beta B N^{\gamma_N} e^{P_{\text{post}}/\gamma_{\text{post}}}}{\gamma_D C_T}\right)^{1/(\gamma_D + \beta)}$. Note the sign: the exponential in the numerator grows with `p_post`.
A check: $D_{\text{crit}}$ for $N = 30$M at 5 bits is about $4.79 \times 10^{11}$ tokens, and one more bit multiplies it by about 5.4.
